thesis: The speakers argue that the history of deep learning is defined by scaling compute, noting that modern models can access a million-fold increase in compute compared to the AlexNet era. They propose that this new compute capacity is best utilized by moving beyond language models to build world models capable of spatial intelligence and processing visual and world data.
